description: Testbenches shipped for T1 item 9. The cocotb stream bench (test_fft256_stream.py) drives the streaming wrapper over the generated core and checks it bit-exactly against the bit-accurate model, plus handshake (including the in_ready and out_valid equations against the core valid), back-pressure, reset mid-frame and zero model overflow, with a negative control (fft-bench-negctl). The remaining listed benches are the existing item 9 evidence: the model and reference tests, the generated-core smoke, the no-overflow amplitude sweep and the candidate growth-schedule sweep, the tests of the shared append-only evidence writer (sim/test_records.py, which also covers the smoke writer through its path parameter), and the per-size model tests (sim/test_model_sizes.py). The list also hashes the files the cold_start targets execute around those benches: sim/__init__.py (every -m sim.* invocation imports the package through it), verification/negctl.sh (shared runner for every *_negctl target), verification/requirements.txt (the venv cold_start builds from; the pins block below is copied from the inventory, not measured from the host, so an unlisted requirements bump would change the environment a recorded pass ran in without drifting anything), verification/flow_tools.py (imported transitively during cold_start: make fxp-model runs sim.test_records, which imports verification/test_fft256_smoke.py, which imports flow_tools; only flow_tools' module body executes inside this argv - its functions belong to the smoke-fft256 flow, which is not in the argv - so within a recorded pass a change to its function bodies does not alter the outcome, but a module-body or import-surface change would, and the file is part of the executed chain either way) and verification/toolchain.json (read at import time by flow_tools.py's module-level PINS assignment; it is the single source of the pins block below and also carries liberty_corner, liberty_file and liberty_relpath, the corner every timing claim must name). cold_start runs every bench and negative control from that venv (see verification/README.md); it is local_only because it needs Icarus, so the signoff.yml runner skips it under --check and re-verifies the recorded hashes. Supersedes manifests/item9-inventory-4.json and its attestation manifests/item9-attestation-4.json (recorded evidence, kept unchanged): -4 hashed the smoke bench's own module but not the two repo files its import surface loads during the same cold_start argv, so an edit to verification/flow_tools.py or verification/toolchain.json passed every signoff gate while a recorded cold_start pass stood (issue #129's drift probe); both join the list here, and .github/workflows/signoff.yml now re-verifies this pair under --check. -4 in turn supersedes manifests/item9-inventory-3.json and its attestation manifests/item9-attestation-3.json (recorded evidence, kept unchanged): -3's testbenches predated the fxp-model target growing to sim.test_overflow_range, sim.test_schedule_sweep and sim.test_model_sizes, and predated sim/__init__.py (added by issue #84's sys.path-bootstrap retirement) and the negctl.sh single-sourcing of PR #95, so a cold_start pass of record was attested over files the inventory did not hash; those files joined the list in -4. The generated core (rtl/generated) and the streaming wrapper (rtl/wrapper) are deliberately not listed: the core is regenerated from the pinned generator and rtl/params/fft256.params (listed), and the benches' verdict is bit-exactness against the hashed model, not a hash of the DUT sources.
